Subject: Re: Lumina: follow-up + eval pack and next steps — technical on pin/rollback

Hi Sanjay — Monica here (SE). Short answers + recommended workflow based on similar customers: 

1) Pinning & artifact integrity:
   • Redwood can pin to an immutable model artifact id (example: gptx-13b-quant-v1@sha256:3a9f...). We include the SHA256 in the manifest and return it via the API metadata. That checksum can be asserted by your runtime.
   • We can additionally publish a signed release manifest (signed by Redwood's release key) — you can verify signature to ensure artifact provenance.

2) Safe upgrade pattern (recommended):
   a) Stage: deploy candidate version to a staging pool and run the eval harness against your prompt set (we can replay traffic and compare metric deltas).
   b) Regression gating: automated check that 95% of your critical prompts do not degrade above an agreed threshold (delta in F1/ROUGE/subjective pass rate).
   c) Canary: small % of production traffic with automated rollback to pinned artifact on regression detection.

3) Escrow/proof-of-state: 
   • For enterprise contracts we offer a 30/90-day artifact escrow snapshot on request (artifact tarball + prompt set + seeds + model-diff reports).
   • We can bind an SLA that enforces rollback/fallback windows and notify both sides via webhook.

4) Quick mitigation options if an unexpected regression lands:
   • Immediate API-level pin to previous artifact (fastest).
   • Traffic route to lower-cost compatible variant (e.g., light-7b-int8) until the candidate is fixed.

Attached a short excerpt showing an example model-diff report (the PDF) and a CSV of the seed prompts + baseline metrics. Our proposal for Lumina: pin production to gptx-13b-quant-v1@sha256:3a9f... and run weekly gated evaluations for the first 60 days post-launch.

If that sounds reasonable I’ll prepare the technical appendix for the contract (artifact manifest, signed releases, webhook spec).

—Monica
